_doc: HMTc Category 4 (Fruits, Vegetables, and Produce) compiler config for tools/standards/compile-category.mjs. Method v2.0, government-limit-only. Eight taxonomy rows: fresh/frozen fruit, dried fruit, fruit snacks, leafy vegetables other than spinach, spinach, non-root vegetables, root and tuber vegetables, and pickled/fermented/brined vegetables. Produce is the most densely regulated food domain in the register: EU Reg. 2023/915 and its Swiss mirror (VHK 817.022.15), EU Reg. 2024/1987 for nickel, Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2, AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19, MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 with its Paraguayan enactment, and Israel MOH FCS-2016 all publish per-produce-class maximum levels for lead and cadmium, and between them cover total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury and nickel. Every number in this config is a named register row; no cell is occurrence-derived, and no percentile, occurrence floor, precautionary adjustment or feasibility adjustment is used anywhere. BASIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING DISCIPLINE FOR THIS CATEGORY: the five fresh rows and the drained pickled row sit in a wet-weight edible-portion as-sold basis and take wet-weight, portion-ordinarily-consumed and as-sold maximum levels at face value; dried fruit and manufactured fruit snacks sit in a dry or concentrated as-offered basis and may name ONLY maximum levels written in that basis, enforced mechanically by a basis_guard, because converting a fresh wet-weight maximum level to a dry basis would require an invented reconstitution factor and Method v2.0 confines reconstitution conversion to infant formula. STAFF / HMTc content, not public wiki (CLAUDE.md Part 19 firewall).

_category.name: Fruits, Vegetables, and Produce
_category.anchor: Per-produce-class sovereign maximum levels for lead and cadmium (EU Reg. 2023/915 and Switzerland VHK 817.022.15; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2; AU-NZ Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016), nickel under EU Reg. 2024/1987, total and inorganic arsenic under MERCOSUR and Israel MOH FCS-2016, and total mercury under Hong Kong Cap. 132V and Israel MOH FCS-2016.
_category.basis_family: dietary as-sold; fresh and frozen produce and drained pickled product on a wet-weight edible-portion basis, dried fruit and manufactured fruit snacks on a dry or concentrated as-offered basis that is never conflated with the fresh wet-weight maximum levels
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only; the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for the row's product form in the row's native basis, a disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination, or a control; never occurrence-derived)
_category.method_note: CELL RESOLUTION RULE, applied uniformly across all eight rows. (R1) Where a credible sovereign government writes a maximum level for this product form in this row's native basis, the cell is the strictest such value and is tagged regulatory-alignment. (R2) Where the exact cell is unregulated but a credible sovereign writes a maximum level for the SAME commodity in an adjacent form or basis, the cell is a disclosed read-across from that named row, taken at face value only where face value is the conservative (stricter) direction. (R3) Where no sovereign instrument reaches the commodity at all, the cell is a CONTROL: testing is mandatory, an escalation rule is published, and no number is invented. Aluminium is a control in all eight rows because no jurisdiction regulates aluminium as a produce contaminant. Hexavalent chromium is a substantiated not-material determination wherever a total-chromium parent is published for the row and a control wherever it is not; it is never a published number. Methylmercury is a CONTROL in all eight rows, bounded by identity below each row's published total-mercury ceiling (methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury), and it is never a published number. No sovereign government writes a methylmercury maximum level for any terrestrial plant food, but the routed corpus contains quantified methylmercury in edible plant and fungal tissue (wang2021-houttuynia-mercury-china in leaf and root tissue of an edible leafy vegetable; stasinos2014-heavy-metals-tubers-review in root and tuber tissue; asensio2023-madrid-mushrooms-mercury), so the species is not absent from produce and no not-material determination is supportable anywhere in this category. Control is the fail-safe treatment and is applied uniformly: a fresh commodity and its dried, manufactured and pickled derivatives are treated alike, so no row is granted a weaker determination than the fresh row it derives from. TAXONOMY LUMPING IS DISCLOSED, NOT SILENTLY RESOLVED: several sovereign instruments split classes that this taxonomy carries as a single row (fruiting versus bulb versus brassica versus legume vegetables inside non-root-vegetables; temperate versus tropical roots and tubers inside root-tuber-vegetables; table olives versus pickled cucumbers versus fermented brassicas inside pickled-fermented-vegetables; pome, stone, citrus and berry fruit inside fresh-fruit). Because one published HMTc value must be met by every product in the row, each such row binds the strictest value applicable to any member, which is materially stricter than law for the looser members. Every collapsed split is named in that row's scope_note, and the recommended taxonomy splits are recorded as outstanding items rather than resolved by picking a looser residual-class value, which would let HMTc certify a lot that is unlawful in a market of sale.
_category.credible_note: The default credible-regulator set is widened by four members for this category, each of which contributes a comprehensive per-commodity produce contaminant schedule rather than a single opportune entry, and each of which is already treated as credible by the live Category 27, 28 and 29 plant-commodity compilers. Switzerland (VHK 817.022.15, 218 register rows) is an EU-aligned metal and metalloid annex whose per-class produce values mirror EU Reg. 2023/915 and EU Reg. 2024/1987 and which supplies the per-class cadmium and nickel rows that are absent from the register's EU coverage. MERCOSUR (GMC Res. 12/2011, 159 rows) is a supranational bloc instrument with a complete produce schedule for lead, cadmium and total arsenic on a product-as-offered-to-consumer basis, including the register's only dried-fruit maximum levels and its only total-arsenic table-olive row; Paraguay (Decreto 1335/2019, 159 rows) is its national enactment at identical values and is admitted so the audit scan sees the national instrument as well as the bloc resolution. MERCOSUR is not, however, the register's only table-olive source: Hong Kong Cap. 132V supplies the table-olive lead row (400 ug/kg) and Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 the table-olive cadmium row (20 ug/kg), and this config names both as anchors in the pickled-fermented-vegetables row; further table-olive rows exist from GSO, Thailand, Colombia and India and sit outside the admitted set. Israel (MOH FCS-2016, 166 rows) supplies the only inorganic-arsenic maximum level any credible government writes for fruits and vegetables and the only total-mercury and inorganic-arsenic rows for dried fruit. Every anchor in this config remains inside this set, and the audit scan runs across all twelve members. Regulators present in the register but NOT admitted here (China, Thailand, India, Vietnam, Singapore, GSO, Colombia, Panama, Uruguay, Trinidad and Tobago, Philippines, Morocco, Fiji) are not a judgment about their credibility; admitting them is a separate governance decision, and China GB 2762 in particular has no produce rows in the register at all (recorded as a register gap).

fresh-fruit.name: Fresh and frozen fruit
fresh-fruit.native_basis_label: fresh or frozen fruit as sold, wet weight, edible portion after washing and removal of stones, stems and inedible peel
fresh-fruit.scope_note: Whole and cut fresh fruit and individually quick-frozen fruit: pome fruit, stone fruit, citrus, berries and small fruit, grapes, tropical and subtropical fruit, and melons. Freezing does not change the water content materially, so frozen fruit shares the fresh wet-weight basis. OUT OF SCOPE: dried and dehydrated fruit (dried-fruit row, a different basis); fruit snacks, purees, leathers, jams and compotes (fruit-snacks row); fruit juices, nectars and fruit drinks (Category 5 Beverages); canned fruit in hermetically sealed tinplate (Category 7 canned-foods-general, which carries the tin maximum level); table olives (pickled-fermented-vegetables row); fruiting vegetables such as tomato, pepper, aubergine and cucurbits, which are botanically fruits but which every sovereign schedule classes as fruiting vegetables (non-root-vegetables row); tree nuts and dried pulses (Categories 28 and 27); products marketed for ages 0 to 5, which route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule. COLLAPSED SOVEREIGN SPLITS: the sovereign schedules split this row for lead (Hong Kong, Switzerland and MERCOSUR set 200 ug/kg for cranberries, currants, elderberries and strawberry-tree fruit against 100 ug/kg for other fruit) and for cadmium (Switzerland sets 20 ug/kg for pome, stone and citrus fruit, 30 ug/kg for berries and small fruit, 40 ug/kg for raspberries and 50 ug/kg for other fruit). The row binds the strictest member value in each case, so berry and cranberry products certify against a bar stricter than their own sovereign class value.
fresh-fruit.basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|as listed|product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market|as sold|as_sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part
fresh-fruit.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor for this row must sit in a dietary as-sold, wet-weight, edible-part or portion-ordinarily-consumed basis. The guard rejects the register's article and material bases (toy and food-contact migration, textile and leather extraction, fertiliser and growing-media dry matter, colour-additive ingredient specifications, animal-feed 12 percent moisture), any one of which would be a basis conflation if it anchored a food row.

Pb.basis_label: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
Pb.label: Five independent credible regulators converge on 100 ug/kg lead for fresh fruit (Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 9, AU-NZ Schedule 19, Switzerland VHK Obst, MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011 with Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019, Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3); the berry carve-outs at 200 ug/kg are named so the collapsed split is visible.
Pb.substantiation: Direct maximum levels for the exact product form in the row's native basis. The berry and cranberry rows at 200 ug/kg are the government-written carve-outs for the accumulating small-fruit species; because one HMTc value must hold across the whole row, the row binds 100 ug/kg and cranberry, currant and elderberry products certify against a value stricter than their own sovereign class. The AU-NZ row is applied on the fresh basis only; Schedule 19 calculates dried and dehydrated foods on the pre-drying basis, which is why it is not carried into the dried-fruit row. AUDIT DISPOSITIONS (from the broader register review rather than this row's scan, which returned no stricter-unselected rows): two stricter Hong Kong rows exist that are not applicable to fresh fruit. 'Tomatoes, preserved by heat treatment and hermetically sealed' (50 ug/kg) is a heat-sterilised canned tomato product and routes to Category 32 tomato-condiments. 'Canned chestnuts and canned chestnuts puree' (50 ug/kg) is a canned tree-nut product and routes to Category 28. MERCOSUR and Paraguayan 'fruit-based ice cream' rows (lead 70 ug/kg, cadmium 50 ug/kg, total arsenic 100 ug/kg) are a frozen dessert form and are not fresh fruit. FROZEN-DESSERT DISPOSITION (identical wording is used in the fruit-snacks lead and total-arsenic cells, the only other places this category states it): fruit-based ice cream and other frozen desserts are out of scope for Category 4 and NO taxonomy row anywhere in hmtc-v2.json currently receives them. Category 24 (Dairy and Milk Products) has nine subcategories (cow milk; goat/sheep/other ruminant milk; camel milk; cheese; yogurt and cultured dairy; cream; milk powders; condensed and evaporated milks; butter and ghee) and contains no ice-cream or frozen-dessert row, so any statement that these products route to Category 24 is false. The lead and total-arsenic rows are stricter than the fruit-snacks row's published values and are currently orphaned, covered by no HMTc standard; this is logged as an open, human-gated taxonomy gap (a new frozen-dessert subcategory carrying the MERCOSUR and Paraguayan fruit_based_ice_cream lead, cadmium and total-arsenic rows) rather than resolved by sweeping a frozen dessert into a produce row whose basis and product form it does not share.

Cd.basis_label: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
Cd.label: Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 sets 20 ug/kg cadmium for pome fruit, stone fruit, citrus fruit and mango, the strictest sovereign cadmium maximum level applicable to any product in this row; MERCOSUR, Paraguay and Israel set 50 ug/kg for fresh fruit generally.
Cd.substantiation: The Swiss annex mirrors EU Reg. 2023/915 and carries the per-class cadmium rows that the register's EU coverage lacks. Pome, stone and citrus fruit are the largest members of this row by volume, so 20 ug/kg is not a marginal member value. Berries at 30 ug/kg, raspberries at 40 ug/kg and residual fruit at 50 ug/kg are the government-written splits; the row binds the strictest, and those looser classes certify against a stricter bar.

tAs.basis_label: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
tAs.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set total arsenic for fresh fruit, berries and small fruit at 300 ug/kg; Israel MOH FCS-2016 sets 1000 ug/kg for the same commodity class.
tAs.substantiation: Direct total-arsenic maximum levels for fresh fruit in an as-offered basis. Total arsenic is reported for its own sake and is never satisfied by the inorganic-arsenic cell; the inorganic-arsenic species limit for this row (60 ug/kg) is far stricter and is the operative arsenic constraint.

iAs.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 sets the only inorganic-arsenic maximum level any credible government writes for fruits and vegetables (60 ug/kg); the EU, Codex, FDA, AU-NZ, Hong Kong and Swiss instruments set inorganic-arsenic maximum levels only for rice, juices, seaweed and infant food.
iAs.substantiation: Inorganic arsenic is the health-relevant arsenic species and is never satisfied by the total-arsenic cell; both are reported. This value is a direct maximum level for the product class, not a read-across, and it sits well below the total-arsenic ceiling for the same row, so the species cell is the binding arsenic constraint in practice.

tHg.basis_label: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
tHg.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 sets total mercury for fruits and vegetables at 30 ug/kg, the only sovereign total-mercury maximum level whose scope reaches fresh fruit.
tHg.substantiation: Direct maximum level for the commodity class. Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 12 sets a stricter 10 ug/kg but its scope is 'vegetables, other than edible fungi' and does not reach fruit, so it is not applicable to this row; it binds the four vegetable rows and the pickled row instead.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for this product form: the routed corpus reports no methylmercury measurement in this matrix, and the only credible methylmercury maximum levels in force (US FDA CPG 540.600; HK Cap. 132V item 11) are scoped to fish, shellfish and crustaceans, so neither supplies an applicable ceiling for a fruit. Methylmercury is therefore held under mandatory analytical control rather than recorded not-material, and it remains bounded by identity below the published total-mercury ceiling for this row (methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury). No methylmercury ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Methylmercury by GC-ICP-MS or EN 16801, required only on a lot whose total mercury reaches 60 percent of the published total-mercury ceiling; any quantifiable methylmercury on such a lot is investigated and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for fruit. EU Reg. 2024/1987, the only comprehensive dietary nickel instrument in existence, enumerates leafy, fruiting, brassica, root, tuber, bulb and legume vegetables, fresh herbs, cereals, pseudocereals, pulses, tree nuts, seeds, cocoa, seaweed and juices, and deliberately sets no maximum level for fruit; the Swiss VHK nickel rows mirror it and likewise omit fruit. Because no instrument reaches the commodity at all, HMTc publishes no nickel number for fresh fruit rather than borrowing the fruiting-vegetable value of 400 ug/kg from a different commodity class.
control.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every lot as part of the mandatory eight-totals panel. Investigate any result above 400 ug/kg (the EU fruiting-vegetable maximum level, used here only as an investigation trigger and not as a certification ceiling) against orchard soil, foliar-spray and stainless-steel processing provenance before release.

not_material.rationale: Every tin maximum level in the register is scoped to canned product: EU Reg. 2023/915 sets 200000 ug/kg for canned foods and 100000 ug/kg for canned beverages, Codex CXS 193-1995 and AU-NZ Schedule 19 set 250000 ug/kg for canned foods, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 250000 ug/kg for canned food other than canned beverages. Those limits regulate one contamination pathway, dissolution of tin from tinplate into the packed food. This row is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that every sovereign tin limit addresses is physically absent and any tin present is dietary background rather than packaging migration. Fresh and frozen fruit is sold loose, in fibre punnets, in film or in polymer trays. Hermetically sealed tinplate presentations of this commodity route to the canned-foods row in Category 7 and carry the canned-foods tin maximum level there.
not_material.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every lot as part of the mandatory eight-totals panel; a result above 50 ug/kg is investigated for a metal-contact source in harvest, wash, transport or packing before the lot is released.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a tin maximum level for non-canned produce; all tin maximum levels in the register are conditioned on a canned (tinplate) presentation, and the EU rows expressly exclude canned dried and canned powdered products from even that scope.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU Reg. 2023/915; EU Reg. 2024/1987 (nickel); Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 (2026 metal/metalloid annex); Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule; AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR, action levels)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or produce form in any jurisdiction. The register's aluminium limits are drinking-water and bottled-water parameters, infant-formula maximum levels, a food-contact plastics specific migration limit, toy migration limits, and permitted-additive levels for baked and starch foods; none of them regulates aluminium as a contaminant of produce. Aluminium is also the third most abundant element in the earth's crust and appears in produce largely as soil-derived and root-associated mineral content rather than as process contamination, so no near-neighbour read-across is supportable either. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone aluminium number for this row.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every lot, reported to the applicant. Document any aluminium-containing processing aid, packaging contact or anti-caking agent, comply with the additive rules of every market of sale, and investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own lot history.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a total-chromium maximum level for this product form. The only dietary total-chromium maximum levels in the register are Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7 for vegetables (500 ug/kg) and pulses, cereals, meat, fish and dairy powder rows under the same item, plus drinking-water and color-additive specifications. The Hong Kong vegetable row does not reach fruit, and no jurisdiction writes a total-chromium maximum level for fruit. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone total-chromium number for this row; total chromium is screened on every lot and hexavalent chromium is controlled by reflex speciation.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot; investigate any elevated result against soil, irrigation water and processing-equipment provenance and reflex-speciate per the Cr-VI control.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any solid food in any jurisdiction: the register's only ingested Cr(VI) parameters are drinking-water maxima (Australia NHMRC 2025, 50 ug/L; California SWRCB, 10 ug/L), which are water-basis parameters that do not reach a solid produce row and whose issuers are not admitted to this category's credible set as food regulators, and every other Cr(VI) row in the register is an article or material limit. This row also has no published total-chromium parent to bound the species against: the only dietary total-chromium maximum level in the register from a regulator in this category's admitted credible set, Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7, is scoped to vegetables and does not reach this product form (the register's remaining dietary total-chromium rows are Chinese GB 2762 milk and milk-powder rows, a different commodity from a regulator outside the admitted set). With neither a species limit nor a published parent, HMTc publishes no hexavalent-chromium number and controls the species by mandatory reflex speciation.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot. Any total-chromium result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation by EN 15192 or EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope dilution; any quantifiable Cr(VI) at LOQ fails the lot and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.
control.bounded_by: Cr (total chromium, itself a control for this row)

dried-fruit.name: Dried fruit
dried-fruit.native_basis_label: dried fruit as offered to the consumer, dry as-sold basis, no reconstitution conversion applied
dried-fruit.scope_note: Sun-dried, tunnel-dried, osmotically dried, freeze-dried and vacuum-dried whole or cut fruit sold as such: raisins and sultanas, prunes, dried apricots, figs, dates, dried apples, dried mango and papaya, dried cranberries and cherries, and freeze-dried fruit pieces. Water content is roughly 15 to 25 percent against 80 to 90 percent for the fresh commodity, so a fresh wet-weight maximum level is between four and six times stricter than its own intent when applied to this row at face value. THE BASIS IS A CONTROLLING FACT FOR THIS ROW, BUT IT IS NOT THE ONLY ONE. Only maximum levels expressed on an as-offered or as-placed-on-market basis are named, enforced by the basis_guard; that admits both an instrument's express dried-commodity rows (Israel's category 3.1 for mercury and arsenic, MERCOSUR's dried-fruits rows for lead and total arsenic) AND an instrument's residual rows whose scope reaches the dried product on that same as-placed-on-market basis, which is how Israel's residual fruits-and-vegetables rows bind the lead and cadmium cells: Israel writes no dried-fruit carve-out in its lead or cadmium tables, so no basis conversion is involved and the residual row governs the dry product as sold. AU-NZ Schedule 19 is expressly excluded, because Schedule 19 calculates dried and dehydrated foods on the pre-drying basis and its fruit lead maximum level of 100 ug/kg is therefore a fresh-equivalent number rather than a dry as-sold number; the row's binding lead value of 100 ug/kg is numerically identical but comes from Israel MOH FCS-2016 on the as-placed-on-market basis, where no conversion is required. OUT OF SCOPE: dried leafy vegetables, dried herbs and dried spices (Category 34); dried mushrooms (Category 29); fruit leathers, strips, purees, gummies and other manufactured fruit confections (fruit-snacks row); dried pulses, nuts and seeds (Categories 27 and 28); products marketed for ages 0 to 5 (Category 1).
dried-fruit.audit_scope: dried fruit|dried fruits|dried vegetables and fruits|trockenfr|getrocknete fr|raisin|sultana|prune|dried apricot|\bdate|\bfig\b
dried-fruit.basis_guard: product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market
dried-fruit.basis_guard_note: This row is a concentrated product in a dry or as-offered basis, so the guard admits only maximum levels expressed for the product as offered to the consumer or as placed on the market and rejects every fresh wet-weight and portion-ordinarily-consumed maximum level. That is deliberate: applying a fresh wet-weight value at face value to a dried product would silently mix bases, and converting between them would require an invented reconstitution factor, which Method v2.0 confines to infant formula.

Pb.basis_label: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
Pb.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 lead category 3 (fruits and vegetables except listed categories, 100 ug/kg, product as placed on market) is the strictest sovereign lead maximum level that reaches dried fruit in this row's own dry as-sold basis; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 write an express dried-fruits lead row at 800 ug/kg, which is named so the government-written dried-fruit split stays visible.
Pb.substantiation: R1 direct maximum level, no basis conversion required. THE ISRAELI INSTRUMENT'S OWN STRUCTURE IS DISPOSITIVE. Israel MOH FCS-2016 writes dried carve-outs where it intends them, and it writes them differently for different analytes: its mercury and arsenic tables carry an express category 3.1 'Dried fruits and vegetables, including mushrooms, edible plants, and herbs' (tHg 150 ug/kg, tAs 5000 ug/kg, iAs 300 ug/kg), which is why those three cells in this row are anchored on the dried category. Its LEAD table carries no dried-fruit category at all: the only lead dried carve-out is category 3.2 'Dried leafy vegetables, celery, mushrooms, edible plants, and herbs' at 1500 ug/kg, which is a Category 34 commodity and out of scope here. Dried fruit therefore falls in the residual lead category 3 'Fruits and vegetables, except listed categories' at 100 ug/kg. That the same instrument excepted dried produce for mercury and arsenic and declined to except dried fruit for lead is the regulator's own choice, not an omission this standard may read in; wiki/regulations/israel-moh-fcs-2016-heavy-metals-tin-food-guidelines.md records the same warning, that several Israeli commodity scopes are broad national categories and downstream standards mapping should use the structured product scope rather than assuming a narrower product row. BASIS. The Israeli row is expressed 'product as placed on market', i.e. the dry product as sold, so it passes this row's basis guard on its own terms and needs no reconstitution factor; the config already treats the identical residual row as an applicable anchor in fresh-fruit Pb and Cd and in non-root-vegetables Cd. This corrects an earlier draft of this cell, which published 800 ug/kg and asserted that stricter fruit lead maximum levels 'are deliberately not carried across the basis change'. That assertion was true of the wet-weight instruments (Hong Kong, AU-NZ, Switzerland and the MERCOSUR fresh-fruit rows, all 100 ug/kg on a fresh basis, all correctly excluded here, and AU-NZ Schedule 19 additionally calculates dried and dehydrated foods on the pre-drying basis) but it was NOT true of Israel, which requires no basis change at all. CONSEQUENCE, DISCLOSED NOT HIDDEN: at 100 ug/kg this row is eight times stricter than the MERCOSUR and Paraguayan dried-fruit lead ceiling, so a raisin lawful at 800 ug/kg in a MERCOSUR market of sale cannot be HMTc certified. That is the government-limit-only method operating as written (strictest applicable sovereign maximum, not the most convenient one), and it is the same over-compliance this category already accepts for the berry, table-olive and brassica members of other rows. The dried/fresh arithmetic argument does not survive contact with the instrument: a dry-basis ceiling written by a sovereign for the dry product as placed on market is not a number 'manufactured by a basis error', it is that sovereign's ceiling.

Cd.basis_label: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
Cd.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 cadmium category 3 (fruits and vegetables except listed categories, 50 ug/kg, product as placed on market) is a direct sovereign maximum level for dried fruit in this row's own dry as-sold basis: Israel's cadmium table carves out dried leafy vegetables and herbs only, so dried fruit sits in the residual row.
Cd.substantiation: R1 direct maximum level. Israel's cadmium table has exactly one dried carve-out, category 3.2 'Dried leafy vegetables, celery, mushrooms, edible plants, and herbs' at 1000 ug/kg, which is a Category 34 commodity; category 3.1 in the cadmium table is 'Leafy vegetables, celery, mushrooms, edible plants, herbs, and horseradish' at 200 ug/kg, not a dried-fruit category. Dried fruit therefore falls in residual category 3 at 50 ug/kg on the product-as-placed-on-market basis, which is the dry product as sold and passes this row's basis guard without conversion. CORRECTION OF RECORD: an earlier draft of this cell resolved as a read-across from the MERCOSUR fresh-fruit cadmium row and justified declining Israel on the ground that 'Israel MOH FCS-2016 lists dried fruits as a separate category (3.1) without a cadmium entry'. That description of the instrument was wrong. The separate dried category 3.1 exists in Israel's mercury and arsenic tables, not in its cadmium table, and it was therefore not a reason to withhold the residual cadmium row. The published number is unchanged at 50 ug/kg because MERCOSUR's fresh-fruit cadmium row carries the identical value, but the provenance is corrected from read-across to regulatory-alignment and the binding jurisdiction from MERCOSUR to Israel, because a direct sovereign maximum level exists and a certification record that misdescribes a cited instrument is impeachable even where the arithmetic survives. MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 writes dried-fruit rows for lead and total arsenic but none for cadmium, and its fresh-fruit cadmium row (50 ug/kg, mercosur_gmc12_2011_fresh_fruits_excluding_berries_small_fruits_cd_50, with the Paraguayan twin) is retained here as numerical corroboration at the identical value rather than as an anchor, since naming a fresh-form row as a direct maximum level for the dried form would be the basis conflation this row's guard exists to prevent.

tAs.basis_label: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
tAs.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set total arsenic for dried fruits at 800 ug/kg; Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3.1 sets 5000 ug/kg for dried fruits and vegetables.
tAs.substantiation: R1 direct maximum levels for the dried commodity on the dry as-sold basis. MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 write an express dried-fruits total-arsenic row at 800 ug/kg and bind this cell; Israel's express dried category 3.1 at 5000 ug/kg is named and is looser. Israel's residual fruits-and-vegetables total-arsenic row (1000 ug/kg) is not the applicable Israeli category here, for the same reason as the inorganic-arsenic cell: Israel writes an express dried category for arsenic. It is looser than the binding value in any event. The inorganic-arsenic species limit for this row (300 ug/kg) is far stricter and is the operative arsenic constraint; total arsenic is reported for its own sake and is never satisfied by the species cell.

iAs.basis_label: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
iAs.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3.1 sets inorganic arsenic for dried fruits and vegetables at 300 ug/kg, the only sovereign inorganic-arsenic maximum level written for a dried produce commodity.
iAs.substantiation: R1 direct maximum level for the dried commodity on the product-as-placed-on-market basis. Israel's residual fruits-and-vegetables inorganic-arsenic row (60 ug/kg) is stricter but is NOT the applicable category: the same instrument writes an express category 3.1 'Dried fruits and vegetables, including mushrooms, edible plants, and herbs' for arsenic, so the dried commodity sits there rather than in the residual row. Both rows sit on the SAME product-as-placed-on-market basis, so the five-fold step between them is the regulator's own treatment of the dried form, not a basis conversion and not an HMTc adjustment. This is the precise contrast that decides the lead and cadmium cells of this same row in the opposite direction: Israel's lead and cadmium tables contain NO dried-fruit category (their only dried carve-out is dried leafy vegetables and herbs), so for those two analytes the residual row is the applicable one and binds at 100 and 50 ug/kg. An instrument that excepts the dried form for three analytes and not for two others has made two different choices, and this row follows each of them where it was made.

tHg.basis_label: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
tHg.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3.1 sets total mercury for dried fruits and vegetables at 150 ug/kg, the only sovereign total-mercury maximum level written for a dried produce commodity.
tHg.substantiation: R1 direct maximum level for the dried commodity on the product-as-placed-on-market basis. The same instrument's residual fruits-and-vegetables row is 30 ug/kg; the five-fold step to the dried category 3.1 at 150 ug/kg is the regulator's own treatment of the dried form, made within a single basis rather than across two, which is why the residual row is not carried into this cell. Where the same instrument writes no dried carve-out at all, as in its lead and cadmium tables, the residual row IS the applicable cell and binds this row at 100 and 50 ug/kg respectively.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for this product form, and no not-material determination is supportable for it: the routed corpus quantifies methylmercury in edible plant and fungal tissue (wang2021-houttuynia-mercury-china measured methylmercury in the leaf and root tissue of an edible leafy vegetable at an LOD of 0.002 ug/kg; stasinos2014-heavy-metals-tubers-review in root and tuber tissue; asensio2023-madrid-mushrooms-mercury), so the species is not absent from produce and the biological premise of a not-material determination is rebutted inside this very category. This row is the concentrated form of the fresh commodity, whose own methylmercury cell is held under the same control; a concentrated derivative is never granted a weaker determination than the fresh row it derives from. Methylmercury is therefore held under mandatory analytical control rather than recorded not-material, and it remains bounded by identity below the published total-mercury ceiling for this row (Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3.1, 150 ug/kg); methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury. control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for fruit in any form, dried or fresh. EU Reg. 2024/1987 enumerates vegetable, cereal, pulse, nut, seed, cocoa, seaweed and juice classes and sets no fruit maximum level at all, and the Swiss VHK nickel rows mirror it. There is therefore no same-commodity value to read across from, and a vegetable wet-weight nickel maximum level could not be carried into this row's dry as-sold basis in any event. HMTc publishes no nickel number for dried fruit.
control.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every lot. Investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own dried-fruit lot history, with attention to stainless-steel dicing and dehydrator contact, and record the drying ratio so results can be compared on a fresh-equivalent basis for surveillance.

not_material.rationale: Every tin maximum level in the register is scoped to canned product: EU Reg. 2023/915 sets 200000 ug/kg for canned foods and 100000 ug/kg for canned beverages, Codex CXS 193-1995 and AU-NZ Schedule 19 set 250000 ug/kg for canned foods, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 250000 ug/kg for canned food other than canned beverages. Those limits regulate one contamination pathway, dissolution of tin from tinplate into the packed food. This row is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that every sovereign tin limit addresses is physically absent and any tin present is dietary background rather than packaging migration. The EU tin maximum levels expressly exclude canned dried and canned powdered products from their own scope, which is the regulator's own recognition that tin dissolution from tinplate is a wet-pack phenomenon; even a canned dried fruit therefore falls outside every sovereign tin maximum level. Hermetically sealed tinplate presentations of this commodity route to the canned-foods row in Category 7 and carry the canned-foods tin maximum level there.
not_material.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every lot as part of the mandatory eight-totals panel; a result above 50 ug/kg is investigated for a metal-contact source in harvest, wash, transport or packing before the lot is released.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a tin maximum level for non-canned produce; all tin maximum levels in the register are conditioned on a canned (tinplate) presentation, and the EU rows expressly exclude canned dried and canned powdered products from even that scope.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU Reg. 2023/915; EU Reg. 2024/1987 (nickel); Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 (2026 metal/metalloid annex); Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule; AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR, action levels)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or produce form in any jurisdiction. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone aluminium number for this row.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every lot, reported to the applicant. Document any aluminium-containing processing aid, packaging contact or anti-caking agent, comply with the additive rules of every market of sale, and investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own lot history.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a total-chromium maximum level for this product form. control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot; investigate any elevated result against soil, irrigation water and processing-equipment provenance and reflex-speciate per the Cr-VI control.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any solid food in any jurisdiction: the register's only ingested Cr(VI) parameters are drinking-water maxima (Australia NHMRC 2025, 50 ug/L; California SWRCB, 10 ug/L), which are water-basis parameters that do not reach a solid produce row and whose issuers are not admitted to this category's credible set as food regulators, and every other Cr(VI) row in the register is an article or material limit. fruit-snacks.name: Fruit snacks
fruit-snacks.native_basis_label: manufactured fruit snack as offered to the consumer, as-sold basis across a wide moisture range (roughly 15 percent for a fruit leather to 80 percent for a puree pouch)
fruit-snacks.scope_note: Manufactured fruit-based snack and spread forms: fruit leathers, strips and rolls, fruit bars whose predominant ingredient is fruit, fruit-puree pouches and cups, fruit gummies and chews formulated from fruit puree or concentrate, and compotes, jellies, jams and marmalades. Products whose predominant ingredient is grain, dairy, nut or confectionery sugar rather than fruit route out (Category 7 snacks-general, Category 33 confectionery, Category 3 grains). Fruit-based ice cream and other frozen desserts are out of scope for this row and no taxonomy row currently exists for them, which is recorded as an open taxonomy gap (see the lead-cell disposition). Fruit juices and nectars route to Category 5. Products marketed for ages 0 to 5, including infant and toddler fruit purees and pouches, route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule, which removes the largest single fruit-puree market from this row. Where MERCOSUR is silent, the cell reads across from a same-commodity fresh fruit-and-vegetable maximum level at face value, which is conservative for the concentrated members of the row and approximately basis-matched for the puree members.
fruit-snacks.audit_scope: jam|jell|marmalade|compote|fruit or vegetable sweet|fruit sweet|fruit snack|fruit leather|fruit bar|fruit pur[eé]e|fruit puree|fruit-based ice cream|fruit based ice cream
fruit-snacks.basis_guard: product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market
fruit-snacks.basis_guard_note: This row is a manufactured product sold across a wide moisture range (roughly 15 percent for a fruit leather to 80 percent for a puree pouch), so the guard admits only maximum levels expressed for the product as offered to the consumer or as placed on the market and rejects every fresh wet-weight and portion-ordinarily-consumed maximum level. That is deliberate: no single fresh wet-weight value can be applied at face value across that moisture range without silently mixing bases, and converting between them would require an invented reconstitution factor, which Method v2.0 confines to infant formula. The guard does not exclude a residual as-placed-on-market row whose commodity scope reaches this product form, which is how the Israeli fruits-and-vegetables rows bind the lead, cadmium, inorganic-arsenic and total-mercury cells here.

Pb.basis_label: manufactured fruit snack as offered to the consumer

Pb.substantiation: R1 direct maximum levels; the row binds the strictest applicable to any member, as this category's cell-resolution rule requires. THE ROW IS WIDER THAN THE MERCOSUR SWEETS CLASS. MERCOSUR's class covers compotes, jellies, jams, marmalades and other fruit or vegetable sweets; this taxonomy row also carries fruit leathers, strips and rolls, fruit bars, fruit-puree pouches and cups, and fruit gummies and chews. Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 9 independently writes jams, jellies and marmalades at 400 ug/kg, corroborating that sovereigns treat this product class as its own cell, but it is deliberately NOT named as an anchor: Cap. 132V expresses every value on a single 'food as listed in the Schedule' basis that the register cannot distinguish from that instrument's fresh wet-weight rows, so it fails this row's basis guard and naming it produces a hard compile failure. It is looser than the binding value in any event. AUDIT DISPOSITIONS: the scan surfaces MERCOSUR and Paraguayan 'fruit-based ice cream' lead at 70 ug/kg. FROZEN-DESSERT DISPOSITION (single wording used in every place this category states it): fruit-based ice cream and other frozen desserts are OUT OF SCOPE for this row and for Category 4 as a whole, and NO taxonomy row anywhere in hmtc-v2.json currently receives them. Category 24 (Dairy and Milk Products) has nine subcategories (cow milk; goat/sheep/other ruminant milk; camel milk; cheese; yogurt and cultured dairy; cream; milk powders; condensed and evaporated milks; butter and ghee) and contains no ice-cream or frozen-dessert row, so the earlier statement that these products 'route to Category 24' was false and has been removed. The consequence is recorded rather than buried: mercosur_gmc12_2011_fruit_based_ice_cream_pb_70 and py_decreto1335_2019_fruit_based_ice_cream_pb_70 (lead 70 ug/kg), the matching cadmium rows at 50 ug/kg, and mercosur_gmc12_2011_fruit_based_ice_cream_tas_100 with its Paraguayan twin (total arsenic 100 ug/kg) are STRICTER than this row's published lead and total-arsenic values and are currently orphaned, covered by no HMTc standard. The broader register review additionally surfaces Hong Kong 'Canned chestnuts and canned chestnuts puree' at 50 ug/kg, a canned tree-nut product routing to Category 28; it was matched only by an over-broad 'puree' token in an earlier draft of this row's audit_scope, which has been narrowed to 'fruit puree' so the scan no longer reports a false positive.

No jurisdiction writes a cadmium maximum level for manufactured fruit snacks specifically: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 writes lead and total arsenic for its fruit-or-vegetable-sweets class but no cadmium row, and Israel writes no jams cadmium row, so every member of this row falls in the Israeli residual fruits-and-vegetables category at 50 ug/kg. An earlier draft resolved this cell as a read-across from mercosur_gmc12_2011_fresh_fruits_excluding_berries_small_fruits_cd_50; the value is unchanged at 50 ug/kg because MERCOSUR's fresh-fruit row carries the identical number, but the provenance is corrected to regulatory-alignment because a direct sovereign maximum level covering this product form exists and does not require a fresh-to-manufactured read-across to reach it. leafy-vegetables-other.name: Leafy and green vegetables other than spinach
leafy-vegetables-other.native_basis_label: fresh or frozen leafy vegetable as sold, wet weight, edible portion after washing and separation of the edible part
leafy-vegetables-other.scope_note: Leaf vegetables and leafy brassicas other than spinach: lettuce and other salad leaves, rocket, chicory, endive, escarole, chard, watercress, lamb's lettuce, and the leafy brassicas (kale, collards, pak choi, Chinese cabbage, mustard greens). Frozen leaf vegetables share the fresh wet-weight basis. THE SPINACH SPLIT IS REAL AND PRESERVED: spinach and similar leaves are excluded here and carry their own row, because EU Reg. 2023/915, Switzerland VHK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V, MERCOSUR and Israel all write spinach out of the general leaf-vegetable class. THE BRASSICA SPLIT IS ALSO A GOVERNMENT SPLIT AND IS HONOURED IN THE SCOPING: head and flowering brassicas (cabbage heads, broccoli, cauliflower, kohlrabi, Brussels sprouts) are NOT in this row; they route to non-root-vegetables, matching Hong Kong's division between 'leafy vegetables including Brassica leafy vegetables' and 'Brassica vegetables other than Brassica leafy vegetables', and Switzerland's division between Blattkohle (leaf cabbages, cadmium 100 ug/kg) and Kohlgemüse (head and flowering brassicas, cadmium 40 ug/kg, expressly excluding Blattkohle). OUT OF SCOPE: fresh culinary herbs and dried herbs and seasonings (Category 34, which is also why the EU and Swiss leaf-vegetable rows named here carry their own 'except fresh herbs' carve-out); edible fungi (Category 29); seaweed and kelp (Category 6); sprouts and microgreens sold as such; dried leafy vegetables (Category 34); products marketed for ages 0 to 5 (Category 1). COLLAPSED SOVEREIGN SPLIT: for lead, AU-NZ Schedule 19 sets 100 ug/kg for vegetables except brassicas and 300 ug/kg for brassicas, so the non-brassica members of this row are held to 100 ug/kg by Australian and New Zealand law while the leafy-brassica members are not. The row binds 100 ug/kg, which is stricter than any instrument applies to kale or pak choi.
leafy-vegetables-other.basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|as listed|product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market|as sold|as_sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part
leafy-vegetables-other.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor for this row must sit in a dietary as-sold, wet-weight, edible-part or portion-ordinarily-consumed basis. The guard rejects the register's article and material bases (toy and food-contact migration, textile and leather extraction, fertiliser and growing-media dry matter, colour-additive ingredient specifications, animal-feed 12 percent moisture), any one of which would be a basis conflation if it anchored a food row.

Pb.basis_label: wet weight, fresh leafy vegetable as sold
Pb.label: AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19 sets lead at 100 ug/kg for vegetables except brassicas, which as a matter of Australian and New Zealand law caps lettuce, rocket, chard and every other non-brassica leaf vegetable in this row; the EU, Swiss, Hong Kong, MERCOSUR, Paraguayan and Israeli leaf-vegetable rows all sit at 300 ug/kg.
Pb.substantiation: The 100 ug/kg value is a direct maximum level applicable to the majority of this row by species count and by volume. It is selected because a published HMTc value of 300 ug/kg would certify a lettuce lot at 250 ug/kg that is unlawful in Australia and New Zealand, which is the failure mode the government-limit method exists to prevent. The consequence is disclosed rather than hidden: the leafy-brassica members of the row (kale, pak choi, collards) are held to a value three times stricter than the 300 ug/kg that AU-NZ, the EU, Switzerland, Hong Kong, MERCOSUR and Israel all apply to them, and the recommended taxonomy fix is a separate leafy-brassica row.

Cd.basis_label: wet weight, fresh leafy vegetable as sold
Cd.label: EU Reg. 2023/915, its Swiss mirror (Blattgemüse and Blattkohle) and AU-NZ Schedule 19 all set cadmium for leaf vegetables at 100 ug/kg; Hong Kong, MERCOSUR, Paraguay and Israel set 200 ug/kg for the same class.

The Swiss Kohlgemüse cadmium row at 40 ug/kg is not named because its own text excludes Blattkohle, so it does not reach the leafy brassicas in this row; it binds the non-root-vegetables row instead, where the head and flowering brassicas sit. That row expressly excludes the leafy brassicas that are the only brassicas in this row, so it is not applicable here; it binds the non-root-vegetables row.

tAs.basis_label: wet weight, fresh leafy vegetable as sold
tAs.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set total arsenic for leaf vegetables at 300 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 2 sets 500 ug/kg for vegetables and Israel MOH FCS-2016 sets 1000 ug/kg.

iAs.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 sets the only inorganic-arsenic maximum level any credible government writes for fruits and vegetables (60 ug/kg); the EU, Codex, FDA, AU-NZ, Hong Kong and Swiss instruments set inorganic-arsenic maximum levels only for rice, juices, seaweed and infant food.
iAs.substantiation: Inorganic arsenic is the health-relevant arsenic species and is never satisfied by the total-arsenic cell; both are reported. tHg.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 12 sets total mercury for vegetables other than edible fungi at 10 ug/kg, the strictest sovereign total-mercury maximum level applicable to this product form; Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 sets 30 ug/kg for the same commodity class.

non-root-vegetables.name: Non-root vegetables (fruiting, brassica, bulb, stem and legume vegetables)
non-root-vegetables.native_basis_label: fresh or frozen vegetable as sold, wet weight, edible portion after washing and separation of the edible part
non-root-vegetables.scope_note: The residual fresh-vegetable row: every vegetable that is neither a root or tuber (its own row) nor a leaf vegetable or spinach (their own rows). It therefore covers fruiting vegetables (tomato, pepper, aubergine, okra and the cucurbits), head and flowering brassicas (cabbage heads, broccoli, cauliflower, kohlrabi, Brussels sprouts), bulb vegetables (onion, shallot, garlic, leek), stalk and stem vegetables (celery, asparagus, fennel, rhubarb, globe artichoke) and fresh legume vegetables (green beans, garden peas, mangetout, fresh edamame in pod). Frozen forms share the fresh wet-weight basis. OUT OF SCOPE: dried pulses and their products (Category 27); sweet corn, which the Swiss and EU fruiting-vegetable lead rows expressly exclude and which routes with cereals to Category 3; edible fungi (Category 29); leafy brassicas such as kale, pak choi and collards (leafy-vegetables-other row, matching the Hong Kong and Swiss leafy-versus-head brassica split); pickled, fermented and brined forms (pickled-fermented-vegetables row); canned vegetables in tinplate (Category 7); vegetable juices (Category 5); products marketed for ages 0 to 5 (Category 1). COLLAPSED SOVEREIGN SPLITS, THE LARGEST IN THIS CATEGORY: every credible instrument subdivides this row, and the subdivisions differ by up to sixfold. For lead, Hong Kong, Switzerland and Israel set 50 ug/kg for fruiting vegetables against 100 ug/kg for bulb, brassica, stem and legume vegetables, and AU-NZ sets 300 ug/kg for brassicas. For cadmium, Switzerland sets 20 ug/kg for fruiting and legume vegetables, 30 ug/kg for bulb and stem vegetables and 40 ug/kg for head and flowering brassicas, while Hong Kong sets 100 ug/kg for legume, stalk and stem vegetables. For total arsenic, MERCOSUR sets 100 ug/kg for bulb, cucurbit, other fruiting and leguminous vegetables and 300 ug/kg for brassicas. For nickel, EU Reg. 2024/1987 sets 400 ug/kg for fruiting vegetables, 500 ug/kg for brassicas, 900 ug/kg for bulb vegetables and 1000 ug/kg for legume vegetables. The row binds the strictest applicable value in each cell, so onions, broccoli and green beans certify against fruiting-vegetable values that no government applies to them. This is the row whose taxonomy split is most worth making.

pickled-fermented-vegetables.name: Pickled, fermented and brined vegetables
pickled-fermented-vegetables.native_basis_label: drained product as sold, wet weight, brine and packing liquid excluded from the analytical portion
pickled-fermented-vegetables.scope_note: Vegetables preserved by acidification, lactic fermentation or brining and sold as such: cucumber pickles and gherkins, sauerkraut, kimchi, pickled onions, beetroot and radish, giardiniera and mixed pickles, olives cured for table use, and pickled peppers. THE BASIS IS THE DRAINED PRODUCT: brine and packing liquid are excluded from the analytical portion, which matches the AU-NZ 'portion ordinarily consumed' construction and the Hong Kong Cap. 132V pickled-cucumber row, and which prevents a lightly-loaded brine from diluting a result. Water content of the drained product is comparable to the fresh vegetable for cucumbers, cabbage and onions, so fresh-basis vegetable maximum levels are comparable at face value; table olives are naturally lower in moisture and carry their own sovereign rows, which are named. OUT OF SCOPE: fermented soy products, soy sauce, fish sauce and vinegar (Category 32); preserved tomato products, including canned and heat-sterilised tomatoes, passata and pickled green tomatoes (Category 32 tomato-condiments), which is why the Hong Kong heat-treated hermetically sealed tomato row at 50 ug/kg is not an anchor here; pickled fruit and chutneys whose predominant ingredient is fruit (fruit-snacks row, or Category 7 for condiment forms); pickled fish and seafood (Category 6); fermented dairy (Category 24); products marketed for ages 0 to 5 (Category 1). Where the certified presentation is a hermetically sealed tinplate can, the canned-foods tin maximum level applies as a hard stop through the tin control below. COLLAPSED SOVEREIGN SPLIT: Hong Kong sets lead at 100 ug/kg for pickled cucumbers and 400 ug/kg for table olives, MERCOSUR and Paraguay set 500 ug/kg for table olives, and Switzerland sets cadmium at 20 ug/kg for table olives with no pickled-vegetable row at all. The row binds the strictest applicable value in each cell, which means the fermented brassica products (sauerkraut, kimchi) are held to a cadmium value written for table olives and the table olives are held to a lead value written for pickled cucumbers. Splitting table olives out of this row is the recommended taxonomy fix.

Pb.basis_label: drained product as sold, wet weight
Pb.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 9 sets lead at 100 ug/kg for pickled cucumbers specifically and for canned vegetables, and Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 20 sets 100 ug/kg for preserved vegetables; the table-olive carve-outs sit at 400 ug/kg (Hong Kong) and 500 ug/kg (MERCOSUR and Paraguay) and the Israeli preserved brassica and leafy row at 300 ug/kg.
Pb.substantiation: Hong Kong writes a pickled-cucumber lead row, so the exact cell is directly regulated for the dominant product form in this row and the cell is a government maximum level rather than a read-across. The row binds the strictest applicable value, 100 ug/kg, and the consequence is disclosed: table olives are held to a value four to five times stricter than the 400 to 500 ug/kg their own sovereign rows allow, reflecting the lye-curing and brine-contact history that those rows accommodate. HONG KONG'S OWN TREATMENT OF THE PICKLED FORM IS THE POINT OF THIS CELL: a pickled cucumber is a cucurbit fruiting vegetable, for which Hong Kong sets 50 ug/kg fresh, yet Hong Kong deliberately writes pickled cucumbers at 100 ug/kg, which is the regulator's own recognition that acidification and brine contact add a pathway the fresh value does not cover. The fresh fruiting-vegetable value is therefore not the applicable cell for this row. AUDIT DISPOSITIONS. This row's audit scan was widened to see the fresh vegetable commodity classes (the same widening that corrected the total-arsenic cell), and it now reports five credible rows at 50 ug/kg, all of them fresh or heat-sterilised forms. Each is dispositioned rather than left silent. (1) hk_cap132v_pb_fruiting-vegetables-cucurbits_50 and (2) hk_cap132v_pb_fruiting-vegetables-other-than-cucurbits_50 are Hong Kong's own FRESH fruiting-vegetable classes. The same instrument separately and expressly writes pickled cucumbers at 100 ug/kg and canned vegetables at 100 ug/kg, so Hong Kong has itself ruled that the preserved form is not governed by its fresh classes; both of the express preserved-form rows are named in this cell. (3) il_fcs2016_pb_3_4_fruiting_vegetables_including_tomato_cucumber_pepper_50 is Israel's fresh fruiting-vegetable category. Israel likewise writes an express preserved-form carve-out, category 20 'Canned vegetables, except listed categories' at 100 ug/kg and category 20.1 'Canned brassica and leafy vegetables' at 300 ug/kg, and this cell names category 20; the canned and jarred presentations that make up this row therefore sit in category 20 under Israeli law, not in the fresh category 3.4. (4) hk_cap132v_pb_tomatoes-preserved-by-heat-treatment-and-hermetically-s_50 governs heat-sterilised canned tomato product, not acidified, fermented or brined vegetables; preserved tomato products including canned tomatoes, passata and pickled green tomatoes route to Category 32 tomato-condiments and are expressly out of this row's scope. (5) ch_vhk_2026_pb_fruchtgemuse_50 is the only one of the five that is not disposed of by its own instrument's text, and it is recorded as an open interpretive call rather than passed over. The Swiss VHK 817.022.15 annex writes per-commodity FRESH vegetable classes and, for LEAD, no pickled, brined, fermented or canned vegetable class at all; the annex does write preserved-form rows for other analytes where it intends them (Tafeloliven cadmium 20 ug/kg, which is this row's binding cadmium anchor; Lebensmittelkonserven tin; getrocknete Bohnen nickel), so its silence on preserved vegetables for lead is a gap in coverage rather than an express extension of the fresh class. The value is not adopted because, unlike total arsenic, lead is an analyte on which sovereign regulators HAVE ruled on the pickled and canned form, and they have ruled uniformly: Hong Kong pickled cucumbers 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong canned vegetables 100 ug/kg, Israel canned vegetables 100 ug/kg. Reading the Swiss fresh Fruchtgemuese class onto a brined product would extend an instrument to a form it does not address, against the uniform contrary treatment of the two instruments that do address it, and would publish 50 ug/kg for a product form for which no sovereign anywhere has written a value below 100 ug/kg. THE CONTRAST WITH THIS ROW'S TOTAL-ARSENIC CELL IS DELIBERATE AND IS THE TEST THIS CATEGORY APPLIES: no sovereign writes any pickled-form arsenic value, so for arsenic the fresh commodity class is the only reading available and it is also the conservative one, which is why that cell now binds 100 ug/kg from the MERCOSUR cucurbit and bulb classes. Where sovereigns have ruled on the processed form, the ruling governs; where none has, the commodity class governs. The canned-vegetable rows of Hong Kong and Israel ARE named here, because canned and jarred presentations of sauerkraut and table olives are squarely in this row.

Cd.basis_label: drained product as sold, wet weight
Cd.label: Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 sets cadmium at 20 ug/kg for table olives, the only sovereign cadmium maximum level written for a product form in this row; Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 6 covers the remaining pickled and fermented vegetables through its residual vegetables row at 100 ug/kg.
Cd.substantiation: The Swiss table-olive cadmium row is not an isolated outlier: the same annex sets 20 ug/kg for fruiting vegetables, legume vegetables and pome, stone and citrus fruit, so table olives sit at the schedule's normal level for a fruit-type edible rather than at a specially strict one. Table olives are named in this taxonomy row, so 20 ug/kg is applicable to it and is the strictest applicable value. The five-fold consequence for sauerkraut, kimchi and pickled onions is disclosed, and splitting table olives into their own row is the recommended taxonomy fix.

tAs.basis_label: drained product as sold, wet weight
tAs.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set total arsenic at 100 ug/kg for the Cucurbitaceae and other fruiting-vegetable classes and for bulb vegetables and sheathing leaves, which are the commodity classes of the pickled cucumbers, gherkins, pickled peppers and pickled onions that dominate this row; the same instrument sets 200 ug/kg for roots and tubers, 300 ug/kg for brassica and leaf vegetables and 300 ug/kg for table olives, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 2 sets 500 ug/kg for vegetables. The row binds the strictest applicable value, 100 ug/kg.
tAs.substantiation: R1 direct maximum levels; the row binds the strictest applicable to any member. WHY THE COMMODITY CLASSES REACH THE PICKLED FORM UNDER THIS INSTRUMENT. MERCOSUR writes separate rows where it intends a processed form to have its own value: table olives and tomato concentrates each get one. It writes NO pickled-cucumber, sauerkraut, kimchi or pickled-onion row, and its vegetable classes are written without a 'fresh' qualifier ('fruiting vegetables of the Cucurbitaceae family', 'bulb vegetables and sheathing leaves'), in contrast to its fruit classes, which are expressly 'fresh fruits excluding berries and small fruits'. A pickled cucumber is a fruiting vegetable of the Cucurbitaceae family, so under MERCOSUR it sits in that class at 100 ug/kg, and a pickled onion sits in the bulb class at 100 ug/kg. This is the same canon of construction this category applies to Israel for dried fruit: where an instrument demonstrably knows how to write a carve-out for a processed form and declines to, the commodity class governs. CORRECTION OF RECORD: an earlier draft of this cell published 300 ug/kg on the table-olive rows alone, with Hong Kong vegetables at 500 ug/kg as the only other named candidate. Table olives are one member of this row; the dominant members had no named candidate at all, and the fresh commodity classes three times stricter were named nowhere and dispositioned nowhere. The row's scan could not surface them because its audit_scope carried only pickle, ferment and olive tokens and its exclusion list carried a bare 'fruit' token that also matched 'fruiting vegetables'; both have been widened and narrowed respectively so the scan can now see these rows. CONSISTENCY WITH THIS ROW'S OTHER ARSENIC CELL: the inorganic-arsenic cell already applies exactly this reasoning, reading 60 ug/kg across from the fresh fruits-and-vegetables class on the ground that acidification, fermentation and brining do not create or concentrate arsenic in the drained product. That argument is analyte-level, not species-level, so it applies with identical force to total arsenic; publishing 300 ug/kg for total arsenic while reading 60 ug/kg across for the species was internally contradictory. THE LEAD CELL IS DIFFERENT ON PURPOSE AND THAT IS NOT A CONTRADICTION: there, Hong Kong writes an express pickled-cucumber lead row at 100 ug/kg against its fresh cucurbit value of 50 ug/kg, so a sovereign has expressly ruled that brine contact adds a lead pathway the fresh value does not cover, and the express pickled row is the applicable cell. No sovereign writes any pickled-form arsenic row, so no such ruling exists for arsenic and the commodity class governs. CONSEQUENCE, DISCLOSED: the table-olive members are held at 100 ug/kg against the 300 ug/kg their own MERCOSUR class allows, which is the same strictest-member over-compliance this row already applies to lead (table olives held at the pickled-cucumber value) and cadmium (fermented brassicas held at the table-olive value). Splitting table olives out of this row is the recommended taxonomy fix. Total arsenic is never satisfied by the inorganic-arsenic cell; both are reported, and the 60 ug/kg species value remains the operative arsenic constraint.

read_across.label: No jurisdiction writes an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for pickled, fermented or brined vegetables; the nearest applicable sovereign value is Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 for fruits and vegetables, 60 ug/kg, the only inorganic-arsenic maximum level any credible government writes for this commodity.
read_across.substantiation: R2 disclosed read-across from the same commodity in its fresh form. Acidification, fermentation and brining do not create or concentrate arsenic in the drained product, and the drained-product basis is comparable to the fresh vegetable for the cucumber, cabbage and onion forms that dominate this row, so face value is basis-appropriate rather than an invented conversion. Israel's dried-produce inorganic-arsenic row (300 ug/kg) is not used because this row is not a dried product.

iAs.basis_label: Israel fresh fruits-and-vegetables inorganic-arsenic maximum level applied to the drained pickled product as sold (comparable basis, disclosed)

read_across.label: No jurisdiction writes a total-mercury maximum level for pickled, fermented or brined vegetables; the nearest applicable sovereign value is Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 12 for vegetables other than edible fungi, 10 ug/kg, the strictest sovereign total-mercury maximum level for the underlying commodity.
read_across.substantiation: R2 disclosed read-across from the same commodity in its fresh form, taken at face value on the comparable drained-product basis. Selecting the stricter of the two available vegetable total-mercury values (Hong Kong 10 ug/kg rather than Israel 30 ug/kg) keeps the read-across in the conservative direction.

tHg.basis_label: Hong Kong vegetable total-mercury maximum level applied to the drained pickled product as sold (comparable basis, disclosed)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for this product form, and no not-material determination is supportable for it: the routed corpus quantifies methylmercury in edible plant and fungal tissue (wang2021-houttuynia-mercury-china measured methylmercury in the leaf and root tissue of an edible leafy vegetable at an LOD of 0.002 ug/kg; stasinos2014-heavy-metals-tubers-review in root and tuber tissue; asensio2023-madrid-mushrooms-mercury), so the species is not absent from produce and the biological premise of a not-material determination is rebutted inside this very category. Every fresh vegetable class this row derives from (leafy, non-root and root/tuber) carries quantified methylmercury in the routed corpus and is held under the same control, and no evidence supports asserting that anaerobic brine fermentation is a methylation-free compartment; control is the fail-safe treatment where the affirmative claim is unsupported. Methylmercury is therefore held under mandatory analytical control rather than recorded not-material, and it remains bounded by identity below the published total-mercury ceiling for this row (read-across from Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 12, 10 ug/kg); methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury. No methylmercury ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Methylmercury by GC-ICP-MS or EN 16801, required only on a lot whose total mercury reaches 60 percent of the published total-mercury ceiling; any quantifiable methylmercury on such a lot is investigated and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.

read_across.label: EU Reg. 2024/1987 writes no maximum level for pickled, fermented or brined vegetables; the nearest applicable sovereign value is its fruiting-vegetable row, 400 ug/kg, which governs the cucumbers and peppers that are the dominant raw material of this row and is the strictest nickel value the instrument sets for any vegetable class it contains.
read_across.substantiation: R2 disclosed read-across from the same commodity in its fresh form. The instrument's own bulb (900), brassica (500) and legume (1000) rows are looser and would each be applicable to some member of this row, so selecting the 400 ug/kg fruiting-vegetable value keeps the read-across in the conservative direction and holds the whole row to the strictest class value rather than the loosest.

Ni.basis_label: EU fruiting-vegetable nickel maximum level applied to the drained pickled product as sold (comparable basis, disclosed)

control.rationale: Tin in this row is a packaging-migration analyte rather than a property of the food. Every sovereign tin maximum level in the register is conditioned on a canned (tinplate) presentation, and this row contains presentations at both extremes: table olives and sauerkraut are still widely packed in hermetically sealed tinplate, while pickles, kimchi and giardiniera are predominantly glass-jarred. Because the row's presentation determines whether any sovereign tin limit applies at all, HMTc publishes no standalone tin number for the row and instead makes the screen mandatory with an escalation to the canned-foods maximum level whenever the certified presentation is tinplate.
control.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every lot. Where the certified presentation is a tinplate can or a metal-lined closure, the canned-foods maximum level (EU Reg. 2023/915, 200000 ug/kg) applies as a regulatory hard stop and the lot is additionally tested at end of shelf life; where the presentation is glass, pouch or plastic, any result above 50 ug/kg is investigated for a metal-contact source.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or produce form in any jurisdiction. The register's aluminium limits are drinking-water and bottled-water parameters, infant-formula maximum levels, a food-contact plastics specific migration limit, toy migration limits, and permitted-additive levels for baked and starch foods; none of them regulates aluminium as a contaminant of produce. Aluminium is also the third most abundant element in the earth's crust and appears in produce largely as soil-derived and root-associated mineral content rather than as process contamination, so no near-neighbour read-across is supportable either. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone aluminium number for this row.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every lot, reported to the applicant. Document any aluminium-containing processing aid, packaging contact or anti-caking agent, comply with the additive rules of every market of sale, and investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own lot history.

read_across.label: No jurisdiction writes a total-chromium maximum level for pickled, fermented or brined vegetables; the nearest applicable sovereign value is Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7 for vegetables other than pulses, 500 ug/kg, the only dietary total-chromium maximum level in the register that reaches this commodity.
read_across.substantiation: R2 disclosed read-across from the same commodity in its fresh form, on the comparable drained-product basis, recorded as a screen rather than a protective ceiling. Acidified and fermented matrices are the strongest case in this category for chromium(VI) reduction to chromium(III), which is why the species cell is a substantiated not-material determination controlled by reflex speciation.

Cr.basis_label: Hong Kong vegetable total-chromium maximum level applied to the drained pickled product as sold (comparable basis, disclosed)
Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is recorded as a SCREEN, not a protective ceiling. Dietary chromium is dominated by nutritionally essential Cr(III); the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), controlled separately by reflex speciation. The screen is excluded from the firm-limit count.

not_material.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any solid food in any jurisdiction. The register's only INGESTED Cr(VI) parameters are drinking-water maxima (Australia NHMRC 2025, 50 ug/L, nhmrc2025_crvi_drinking_water_50; California SWRCB, 10 ug/L, us_ca_swrcb_2024_cr-vi_chromium-hexavalent_mcl_10ugl and ca_swrcb_crvi_drinking_water_10), which are water-basis parameters expressed per litre of a consumed liquid and supply no applicable ceiling for a solid produce row in this row's native basis; every remaining Cr(VI) row in the register is an article or material limit (toys, textiles, leather, fertilisers, electrical equipment). Chromium in produce is dominated by nutritionally essential Cr(III), and Cr(VI) is not stable in the plant matrix: fruit and vegetable tissue is an aqueous, organic-acid and ascorbate-rich reducing medium in which Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III), so a reported Cr(VI) value in this matrix reflects extraction conditions rather than the chromium species the consumer ingests. Hexavalent chromium is therefore bounded by the published total-chromium screen for this row (read-across from Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7, 500 ug/kg) and controlled by reflex speciation rather than by a published number.
not_material.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot. Any total-chromium result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation by EN 15192 or EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope dilution; any quantifiable Cr(VI) at LOQ fails the lot. Cr(VI) is never published as a panel number.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a Cr(VI) maximum level for any solid food. The register's ingested Cr(VI) parameters are drinking-water maxima only (AU NHMRC 50 ug/L; California SWRCB 10 ug/L), which are water-basis and do not reach produce; every other Cr(VI) row is an article or material limit (EU 2009/48 toys, EU 2018/1513 textiles, EU 301/2014 leather, EU 2019/1009 fertilisers, EU RoHS). Neither drinking-water issuer is admitted to this category's credible set as a food regulator for a solid produce row. The total-chromium parent for this row is published.
